title: Malaysian Hainanese Chicken Chop with Brown Gravy & Fries
dek: Craggy, juicy fried chicken cutlets are paired with crisp oven fries, a smooth onion-Worcestershire brown gravy and cool cabbage salad for a complete Malaysian kopitiam-style dinner.
image_alt: Craggy breaded Malaysian Hainanese chicken chop with fries, smooth brown gravy, cabbage salad and a tomato wedge on a white plate
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb russet potatoes, scrubbed and cut lengthwise into 1/2-inch fries
5 tbsp neutral oil, divided, plus about 1 1/2 cups for shallow-frying
2 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
4 boneless, skinless chicken thighs (about 6 oz each), trimmed
1 medium yellow onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
1 large ripe tomato, cut into 4 wedges

instructions.name: Heat the oven and start the fries
instructions.text: Set a rack in the upper third of the oven and heat to 450°F. Cover the cut potatoes with cold water for 10 minutes, drain and dry very thoroughly. Toss with 2 tablespoons neutral oil, 3/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Spread cut-side down on a large rimmed sheet pan with space between the pieces. Roast for 20 minutes before turning.

instructions.name: Make the cool cabbage salad
instructions.text: While the potatoes begin roasting, toss the cabbage, carrot, mayonnaise, rice vinegar, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, 1/4 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a bowl. Refrigerate while the hot components cook; the short rest softens the cabbage slightly without making it limp.

instructions.name: Flatten and season the chicken thighs
instructions.text: Place each chicken thigh between two sheets of parchment and pound the thickest areas to an even 1/2 inch. Combine 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce and the garlic powder, rub it over all sides and stand for 10 minutes. Wash and sanitize the work surface and any tool that touched raw chicken before continuing.

instructions.name: Build the three-part breading station
instructions.text: Put 1/2 cup flour in a shallow bowl. Whisk the eggs with 2 tablespoons water in a second bowl. Put the panko in a third. Pat excess marinade from one thigh, coat it lightly in flour, dip in egg and press firmly into the panko so the surface is completely covered. Repeat with the remaining thighs and let the breaded pieces stand on a rack for 8 to 10 minutes so the coating hydrates and adheres.

instructions.name: Turn and finish the oven fries
instructions.text: Turn each fry with a thin spatula and return the pan to the upper rack for 15 to 20 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp at the edges. Toss immediately with 1/4 teaspoon salt. If the fries finish before the chicken, hold them uncovered in a 225°F oven so steam does not soften them.

instructions.name: Cook the smooth brown gravy
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon neutral oil and the butter in a 2-quart saucepan over medium. Add the onion and 1/4 teaspoon salt; cook for 7 to 9 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the remaining 1/4 cup flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the chicken broth, then add the ketchup, 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, white pepper and remaining 1/2 teaspoon sugar. Simmer for 5 to 7 minutes, whisking often, until the gravy coats a spoon. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, or carefully use a countertop blender with the center cap vented. Return to low heat and adjust with water 1 tablespoon at a time if it becomes thicker than pourable gravy.

instructions.name: Shallow-fry the chicken chops in two batches
instructions.text: Pour 1/2 inch neutral oil into a 12-inch heavy skillet and heat over medium-high to 350°F. Lower two breaded thighs away from you and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, adjusting the heat to keep the oil between 325°F and 350°F. Transfer to a wire rack over a sheet pan and check the thickest center with an instant-read thermometer; it must reach at least 165°F. Repeat with the other two thighs, letting the oil return to 350°F first. If any piece is below 165°F, finish it on the rack in a 375°F oven and recheck.

instructions.name: Plate the photographed kopitiam-style meal
instructions.text: Rest the chicken for 5 minutes. Divide the crisp fries and chilled cabbage salad among four plates and add one tomato wedge to each. Place one whole breaded chicken chop beside them and serve about 1/3 cup smooth brown gravy in a small heatproof cup or ramekin so the crust stays crisp, matching the verified photograph. Serve the remaining gravy at the table.

why_it_works: Chicken thighs stay juicy under the craggy coating, while pounding their thickest sections creates an even profile that fries through before the crumbs overbrown.
Flour gives the egg a dry surface to grip, egg binds the coarse panko and a short rack rest hydrates the layers so fewer crumbs shed into the oil.
Holding the frying oil within a measured 325–350°F range lets the coating set quickly without leaving the center undercooked or the crust greasy.
A lightly browned onion-and-flour base gives the gravy body; blending makes it smooth enough for the separate sauce cup visible in the verified photograph.
Serving the hot gravy apart from the chicken protects the crisp crust, while cool tangy cabbage and tomato balance the fried cutlet and fries.
swaps: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts can replace thighs. Slice two large breasts horizontally into four cutlets, pound to 1/2 inch and still verify 165°F in the thickest center.
For a less craggy crust, replace panko with 1 1/2 cups fine dry breadcrumbs. The coating will be more compact but the same three-stage breading method applies.

For an air-fryer variation, spray both sides of the breaded thighs thoroughly with oil and cook in a single layer at 390°F for 12 to 16 minutes, turning once and verifying 165°F. This is a useful variation, not the fried finish shown in the photograph.
Use apple-cider vinegar in the cabbage salad if rice vinegar is unavailable; begin with 2 teaspoons because it can taste sharper.
Vegetable broth can replace chicken broth in the gravy, but use a full-flavored low-sodium brand and adjust the final seasoning after simmering.
storage: Refrigerate chicken, fries, gravy and cabbage salad in separate shallow containers within 2 hours. Keep chicken, fries and gravy for up to 4 days and the salad for up to 3 days. Reheat chicken and fries uncovered on a rack in a 375°F oven until crisp and the chicken reaches 165°F; bring the gravy to a boil in a small saucepan, whisking in a splash of water as needed. Do not reheat the cabbage salad. Freeze cooked chicken chops individually for up to 1 month and thaw overnight in the refrigerator; the gravy can be frozen separately for up to 2 months.
notes: Malaysia's official tourism site identifies Hainanese chicken chop as a traditional local favorite, and the verified Commons description connects the dish to Hainanese cooks adapting Western techniques in Malaysian kopitiams. This recipe presents that Malaysian fusion style rather than Hainanese chicken rice.

USDA guidance requires all poultry pieces to reach 165°F and leftovers to be reheated to 165°F. Crust color cannot confirm the temperature of a folded chicken thigh, so probe the thickest center of every batch.

The CC BY-SA 4.0 photograph was inspected at full size before publication. It clearly shows a large craggy breaded chicken chop, fries, smooth brown gravy in a separate cup, cabbage salad and a tomato wedge; the title, method, plating direction and alt text are limited to those visible components.

Keep the gravy pourable rather than pasty: it should coat a spoon but flow cleanly into a ramekin. Broth reduction and flour brands vary, so the final tablespoons of water are an intentional adjustment.

The 95-minute total includes the breading rest, chicken rest and overlapping prep. An organized cook can make the salad and bread the chicken while the fries roast, then finish the gravy while the coating rests.

Calories and cost estimate one breaded chicken thigh, one-fourth of the fries and salad, about 1/3 cup gravy and a tomato wedge. Frying-oil absorption is estimated; most of the measured oil remains in the skillet.

faqs.q: How do I keep the breading attached to the chicken chop?
faqs.a: Dry the marinated surface before flouring, cover every patch in the flour-egg-panko sequence and let the coated thighs rest on a rack for 8 to 10 minutes. Lower them gently into fully heated oil, turn only after the first side has set and use tongs at the edge rather than squeezing the broad crust.

faqs.q: Can I pour the brown gravy over the chicken before serving?
faqs.a: You can, but the crust softens quickly. The verified presentation keeps the smooth gravy in a small cup, which lets each diner dip or spoon it onto individual bites while the remaining cutlet stays crisp. If you prefer a sauced chop, pour it only at the table.

faqs.q: Can the chicken chops be prepared ahead for a dinner party?
faqs.a: Bread them up to 4 hours ahead, arrange them in one layer on a rack, cover loosely and refrigerate. Fry just before serving for the best crust. If they must be cooked ahead, cool on a rack and reheat at 375°F until crisp and 165°F in the center; warm the gravy separately and keep the salad cold.
